findings.summary: AArch64 is the 64-bit execution state of the ARM architecture, introduced with ARMv8-A in 2011 and carried forward into ARMv9-A. It provides 31 general-purpose 64-bit registers and a distinct A64 instruction set, while maintaining backward compatibility with 32-bit AArch32 state and its A32/T32 instruction sets. The architecture supports advanced SIMD (Neon) with 32 registers, IEEE 754 floating-point, and cryptography extensions. It was designed to enable 64-bit memory addressing and performance improvements alongside existing 32-bit software through dual-state processors.

mechanisms.title: Dual execution state support
mechanisms.explanation: Processors implement both AArch64 (64-bit) and AArch32 (32-bit) execution states, allowing the same core to run 64-bit and 32-bit code. The execution state is selected at exception level and can be mixed, with 32-bit applications executing under a 64-bit OS or hypervisor.

mechanisms.title: A64 instruction set and register file
mechanisms.explanation: AArch64 introduces the A64 instruction set with 31 general-purpose 64-bit registers (x0-x30, where x31 is the stack pointer or zero depending on mode) and 32 × 128-bit SIMD/Neon registers. The program counter is not directly addressable, and most instructions accept 32-bit or 64-bit operands with 64-bit addresses.
